findings.who: A filer whose 2022 American opportunity credit was removed by an automated IRS notice, for example a CP-series letter saying the student was not eligible or the four-year limit was reached. The notice adjusted the return without a formal audit.
findings.why_no: The question excludes a denial 'for a math or clerical error'. A filer cannot tell how the IRS classified an automated notice, so they may read any computer-generated notice as a math or clerical correction and answer No.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1, Form 8862 may be required: "If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015, you must attach a completed Form 8862"
findings.fix: Ask about facts the filer can check: 'Since 2016, has the IRS sent you (or your spouse) a notice or audit report that removed or lowered an American opportunity credit?' After a Yes, explain that a pure arithmetic or copying correction does not count, and that a change because the student, expenses or credit did not qualify does count. Tell the filer to answer Yes when unsure.

findings.who: A filer who got an audit letter about their American opportunity credit and agreed to the change by signing an examination report, or who sent an amended return giving up the credit in response to the IRS.
findings.why_no: They read 'Has the IRS ever denied or reduced' as an IRS decision imposed on them. Because they conceded or withdrew the credit themselves, they do not see it as a denial.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1, Form 8862 may be required: "If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error ... you must attach a completed Form 8862 ... to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit"
findings.fix: Add to the question or help: 'Count it even if you agreed to the change, did not respond, or gave up the credit on an amended return after IRS contact.'

findings.who: A filer whose 2024 American opportunity credit was disallowed in an IRS notice of deficiency or examination, and who has an appeal or Tax Court case still pending when they file the 2025 return.
findings.why_no: They treat the disallowance as not yet final ('the IRS hasn't decided') and answer No while the dispute is open.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1, Form 8862 may be required: "If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced ... you must attach a completed Form 8862 ... to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit"
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Count a denial or reduction even if you are appealing it or it is still under review.'

findings.who: A filer whose American opportunity credit for an ex-spouse, or claimed on a joint return with an ex-spouse, was denied in 2019. They now file jointly with a new spouse.
findings.why_no: 'An American opportunity credit you ... claimed' reads to them as the ex-spouse's credit, since the student or the paperwork was the ex's. 'Your spouse' points to the current spouse, so they answer No.
findings.irs_text: i8863 p. 1, Form 8862 may be required: "If your American opportunity credit was denied or reduced for any reason other than a math or clerical error for any tax year beginning after 2015, you must attach a completed Form 8862"
findings.fix: Add: 'Include a credit claimed on any earlier return you signed, including a joint return with a former spouse, and any earlier return your current spouse signed.'

locators: p. 3, American Opportunity Credit, "Caution: Don’t claim the American opportunity credit for 2 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to reckless or intentional disregard of the rules or 10 years after there was a final determination that your claim was due to fraud."; p. 1, Form 8862 may be required, "you must attach a completed Form 8862, Information To Claim Certain Credits After Disallowance, to your tax return for the next tax year for which you claim the credit"
